lesson.intro: An adjective is a describing word. It tells us more about a noun: its [[colour]], [[size]], [[shape]], [[feeling]], [[taste]] or [[number]].
points: Colour: red, blue, green. Size: big, tiny, tall. Shape: round, square.
Feelings: happy, sad, angry. Taste: sweet, sour, salty. Number: one, three, many.
An adjective usually comes before a noun (a [[red]] apple) or after "is/are" (The apple is [[red]]).
To compare two things, add -er + than: tall → [[taller]] than. For long words use more: [[more beautiful]] than.
To compare three or more, use the + -est: the [[tallest]]. For long words use most: the [[most beautiful]].
Some adjectives change completely: good → better → best; bad → worse → worst.

examples.text: Mount Kinabalu is the [[highest]] mountain in Malaysia.
This is the [[most interesting]] book I have read.

lesson.tip: Short word ending consonant-vowel-consonant? Double the last letter: big → bigger → biggest. Ending in y? Change y to i: happy → happier → happiest.
